library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
# Define file paths
files <- list(
  wave1 = "data/input/wave_one_lsype_young_person_2020.tab",
  wave2 = "data/input/wave_two_lsype_young_person_2020.tab",
  wave3 = "data/input/wave_three_lsype_family_background_2020.tab",
  wave4 = "data/input/wave_four_lsype_family_background_2020.tab"
)

# Helper to map each wave variable to standard codes
map_lang <- function(df, var_name, var_type){
  # Map missing codes to NA, keep substantive 1-4
  # YP variables: -99, -92, -91, -1 -> NA (missing codes) etc.
  if(var_type == "YP"){
    df %>% mutate(!!sym(var_name) := case_when(
      !!sym(var_name) %in% c(-99, -92, -91, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      !!sym(var_name) %in% c(1,2,3,4) ~ !!sym(var_name),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ))
  } else if(var_type == "HH"){
    df %>% mutate(!!sym(var_name) := case_when(
      !!sym(var_name) %in% c(-999, -997, -99, -92, -91, -1) ~ NA_real_,
      !!sym(var_name) %in% c(1,2,3,4) ~ !!sym(var_name),
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    ))
  }
}

# Load wave 1
wave1 <- read_delim(files$wave1, delim = "\t", col_types = cols(.default = col_double(), NSID = col_character()))
# rename variable
wave1 <- wave1 %>% rename(w1_var = W1englangYP)
# map
wave1 <- map_lang(wave1, "w1_var", "YP")

# Load wave 2
wave2 <- read_delim(files$wave2, delim = "\t", col_types = cols(.default = col_double(), NSID = col_character()))
wave2 <- wave2 %>% rename(w2_var = W2EnglangYP)
wave2 <- map_lang(wave2, "w2_var", "YP")

# Load wave 3
wave3 <- read_delim(files$wave3, delim = "\t", col_types = cols(.default = col_double(), NSID = col_character()))
wave3 <- wave3 %>% rename(w3_var = W3englangHH)
wave3 <- map_lang(wave3, "w3_var", "HH")

# Load wave 4
wave4 <- read_delim(files$wave4, delim = "\t", col_types = cols(.default = col_double(), NSID = col_character()))
wave4 <- wave4 %>% rename(w4_var = W4EngLangHH)
wave4 <- map_lang(wave4, "w4_var", "HH")

# Merge all waves
merged <- full_join(wave1, wave2, by = "NSID") %>%
  full_join(wave3, by = "NSID") %>%
  full_join(wave4, by = "NSID")

# Consolidate language variable
merged <- merged %>%
  mutate(lang = case_when(
    !is.na(w1_var) ~ w1_var,
    !is.na(w2_var) ~ w2_var,
    !is.na(w3_var) ~ w3_var,
    !is.na(w4_var) ~ w4_var,
    TRUE ~ -3
  ))

# Select only ID and consolidated var
final_df <- merged %>% select(NSID, lang)

# Write to CSV
write_csv(final_df, "data/output/cleaned_data.csv")

   - The two primary structures are:
     a. **One consolidated variable** — a single value per person across all waves. Used for stable or time-invariant constructs such as sex, ethnicity, or language.
     b. **Separate wave-specific variables** — one variable per person per wave, named with an age suffix. Use for time-varying constructs such as economic activity, partnership status, or income.
   - Base this decision on the construct, metadata labels, available waves, and additional requirements.
   - Where the same construct applies to multiple subjects (e.g., mother and father), create parallel sets of variables — one per subject — following the same a/b structure.
   - If waves have different levels of response detail and comparability is required, create both collapsed harmonised variables (consistent categories across waves) and detailed wave-specific variables.
   - If the task requires variables measuring genuinely distinct dimensions of the same construct — not just different levels of detail — create a separate variable per dimension. Examples: academic vs vocational qualifications; item-summed vs caseness scores.
